comment: K1061 supplied the decisive scoped preference: at low displacement under shared SGD, residual networks can beat deep plain networks with more LayerNorms when the plain network ends in an unnormalized block. This directly favored B over A. C also lacked residual connections and ended unnormalized, although that comparison was less directly covered by K1061. K1003 established the slow-optimization regime, while K1016 discouraged treating C’s greater width as decisive. The result supports the existing recipe-scoped rule; it does not isolate residual connections from activation, depth, or normalization placement.
